A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same theoretical work despite the title changing from Hard-Attention Transformers to Autoregressive Transformers. All pages, equations, both figures, and Appendices A–D are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: V1 presents mathematical definitions, expressivity results, and proofs, including its appendices. The experiments discussed in Section 6.3.3 are explicitly attributed to Yang et al. (2025), not reported as original experiments.

after.justification: V2 remains theoretical throughout the main text and appendices. Section 5.3.3 retains the discussion of others' experiments, while Section 7 proposes future empirical investigations without reporting outcomes.

M1.justification: The attention mechanism, classifier outputs, normalized autoregressive formulation, and logical constructions are retained. V2's explicit state-encoder definition restates the concept already described in v1 Section 5.

E1.justification: Neither version conducts training or evaluation on datasets or tasks. Formal-language examples remain theoretical; newly cited benchmarks and proposed future scenarios are not evaluated.

E2.justification: Neither version reports empirical baseline comparisons. The transformer, automaton, and logic classes compared theoretically are retained.

E3.justification: Neither version contains an experimental evaluation protocol. Precision, masking, and positional-encoding assumptions describe retained theoretical model classes rather than changed experimental settings.

E4.justification: Neither version reports ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity studies, or empirical case studies. The added appendix proof is a theoretical addition rather than supplementary experimental analysis.

E5.justification: Repeated runs, seeds, uncertainty estimates, and statistical tests are absent from both versions.

E6.justification: No empirical result entries are added or revised. Figure 2 retains its illustrative weights, and the cited depth-k recognition versus symbol-prediction findings in v1 Section 6.3.3 and v2 Section 5.3.3 are unchanged. The new Boolean-equivalence proof supports a fact already stated in v1.

T1.justification: Appendix C adds Proposition C.1 and a subset-construction proof of Boolean counter-free NFA/DFA equivalence, previously stated without this proof. It also removes the explicit weighted-path equality used to justify Figure 2c's counter-freeness. The principal theorems and proofs in Appendices A, B, and D are otherwise retained; the next-symbol and prefix lemmas are relocated and renumbered, not removed.

C1.justification: Both versions claim the same state-encoder equivalences, real-weighted DFA/NFA separation, and selective expressivity increases from autoregression. V2's transfer-oriented framing and PARITY example explain consequences of retained results rather than establish a new central contribution.

C2.justification: V2 replaces the brief conclusion with substantial applicability discussion in Section 7: when recognizer impossibility results transfer, the lack of corresponding tools for real autoregressors, and obstacles involving log-precision attention, positional encodings, and chain of thought. Section 5.2 also corrects the interpretation preceding the retained corollary from autoregressors being generally more powerful to classifiers and autoregressors being incomparable.

D1.justification: Neither version provides implementation instructions, experimental hyperparameters, hardware reports, or code/data-release information. The expanded definitions and proof explanations concern the mathematical framework.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands research positioning. It explicitly credits earlier transformer/automaton state-encoding connections to Liu et al. (2023) and Rizvi-Martel et al. (2024), connects future questions to chain-of-thought theory, and situates the results within a broader formal-language experimental literature. These substantive connections go beyond moving the existing Related Work section.

P1.justification: V2 substantially rewrites the introduction and reorganizes the narrative: Related Work moves from Section 2 to Section 6, Conclusion becomes an expanded Discussion, and formal lemma statements in the main text give way to explanatory proof sketches while remaining in Appendix B. The title, terminology, and several explanatory passages are also revised.

P2.justification: Both figures retain their diagrams and substantive content, and neither version contains tables. V2 introduces blue citation and cross-reference styling and modest typesetting and layout adjustments, without adding or substantially redesigning visual displays.

improvement.justification: V2 improves readability and self-contained support through main-text proof sketches, the Boolean-equivalence proof in Appendix C, clearer prior-work attribution, and specific applicability limits in Section 7. These are useful but bounded gains to the retained theory. Appendix C removes v1's problematic weighted-path equality without explaining how Figure 2c's real-weighted example satisfies Definition C.2, so that theoretical ambiguity remains.
